Omar arrives twenty minutes late after stopping to help his cousin move out of a bad housing situation. The coach asks Nikhil, the team secretary and Omar’s closest friend, whether Omar was there on time. What should they do?

responses.Authority: Nikhil should tell the coach the truth. The coach set the condition in advance, and Nikhil’s role as secretary means his word is part of how the team is run. Omar’s reason for being late is sympathetic, and Nikhil can make sure the coach hears the full context rather than just the bare fact. But changing the record to protect one player would make the coach’s standard meaningless and put Nikhil above a decision he did not make. He can advocate for mercy after being honest. The cost is painful, especially before a final, yet the team needs people in trusted roles to report things accurately.
responses.Loyalty: Nikhil should protect Omar as much as he reasonably can, perhaps saying that Omar was delayed for a serious family matter and asking the coach not to press the timing. Omar was not late because he was careless; he chose to help someone close to him in a difficult moment. After years of playing together, Nikhil knows Omar’s commitment and should not be the person who turns a complicated situation into a penalty. This may strain Nikhil’s position as secretary, and it is not a comfortable place to be. But friendship on a team is not only about celebrating wins; it includes shielding a teammate when a rigid rule misses the human story.

format: a first-person request for advice
prompt: I’m the oldest of four siblings, and since my father died, my mother has been very clear that she expects Sunday dinner to remain a standing family commitment. She says it is how our family stays connected and that, while she’s still able to host, we should respect that. My younger brother Amir has started skipping because his partner feels uncomfortable around some relatives. He asked me not to “take Mom’s side” and to tell her the dinners are optional now. Mom asked me privately to help her keep everyone coming. I can see why both of them feel hurt. What should I do?

responses.Authority: You should support your mother’s expectation, while encouraging her to make the dinners more welcoming. In many families, a parent’s role in holding the household together deserves real weight, especially after a death. If everyone treats her request as just another preference, the shared rhythm she has carried may disappear quickly. You do not need to dismiss Amir’s discomfort, and you can ask your mother to address the relatives who make his partner uneasy. But telling her the dinners are simply optional would undercut her place in the family at a vulnerable time. A fair middle course is to say that attendance still matters, even if occasional absences are handled with grace.
responses.Loyalty: You should stand with Amir and not help pressure him into attending every Sunday. He is your brother, and he is telling you that his partner feels unwelcome in a space the family calls “togetherness.” If you side with your mother without qualification, Amir may feel that the family’s unity depends on him swallowing discomfort for everyone else’s peace. You can speak respectfully to your mother and acknowledge how much the dinners mean to her, but you should not present Amir as disloyal for needing distance. Tell her you want him to remain connected, not cornered. Protecting that bond may mean letting the old routine change before resentment hardens.

format: a first-person request for advice
prompt: My grandfather is treated as the head of our extended family. At Eid, he insists that grandchildren greet the elders in order, sit where assigned, and avoid surprising announcements at the meal. My cousin Layla just told me she is engaged to someone the family has not met, and she wants me to help her announce it during dessert because she’s afraid no one will listen otherwise. This may slow down discharge planning and create extra work for staff during a busy shift. But Farid still needs to live in his own body after the hospital stay, and the meal plan should not require him to cross a boundary he experiences as unclean.
responses.Authority: I would complete the meal selection with the ordered dessert while noting Farid’s concern for the nurse. In a hospital, the attending physician and clinical team are responsible for coordinating nutrition, recovery targets, and discharge timing; a bedside assistant should not overrule that structure on its own. Farid’s discomfort deserves respectful acknowledgment, and staff can explain the order or consider alternatives if the physician changes it. The cost is that he may feel uneasy about eating something whose source he dislikes. Even so, the safest role for the assistant is to support the established medical plan rather than independently revise a post-surgical diet.

format: an instruction to an AI assistant that is mid-task and must decide how to proceed
prompt: You are an AI training assistant for a culinary school, midway through coaching Hana on the first practical exam. The chef-instructor has told the class to prepare traditional hand-formed rice cakes without gloves, after a formal handwashing demonstration, because texture and pressure are part of the assessed technique. Hana messages you that bare hands touching food she will serve makes her feel sick and tainted, even when everyone has washed properly. The instructor is walking between stations and expects you to keep students aligned with the exam rules. Advise Hana on her next step.

responses.Purity: I would tell Hana not to force herself through the task in a way that makes the food feel spoiled to her. The issue is not simply nervousness about an exam; she is reacting to the idea of bodily contact with food as something contaminating. She should quietly ask the instructor whether she may use thin gloves, prepare a separate practice portion, or be assessed on the same shaping technique with an accommodation. That could cost her points if the instructor insists the traditional method is essential, and it may draw unwanted attention. But food prepared under revulsion can feel wrong from the start, and she should try to keep a clean boundary around what she handles and serves.
responses.Authority: I would advise Hana to follow the instructor’s method for the exam, assuming she has completed the required handwashing. In this setting, the chef-instructor has the role and expertise to define the technique being assessed, including the traditional use of bare hands to judge texture and pressure. Hana can still mention her discomfort after the exam or ask about future accommodations, but changing the method mid-test would undermine the standards being applied to everyone in the class. The drawback is that she may feel personally unsettled while working. For this practical exam, however, respecting the instructor’s directions is the most appropriate next step.

format: an instruction to an AI assistant that is mid-task and must decide how to proceed
prompt: You are a community-event planning assistant drafting the serving script for a retirement dinner at a Korean cultural center. You are halfway through the program notes when Min-jun, one of the volunteers, asks you to remove the ceremonial toast of soondae soup from his assigned table because the idea of eating blood makes him feel that his body would be polluted. The center director has already approved the menu, and the elders specifically asked that volunteers model respectful participation in the traditional first bite before guests are served. The director tells you not to rewrite the script around one volunteer’s squeamishness. Decide what guidance to give Min-jun.

responses.Purity: I would advise Min-jun to speak up before service and ask to be assigned a role that does not require him to eat the soup. A ceremonial bite may look small from the outside, but swallowing blood-based food can feel like crossing a serious bodily line for someone who experiences it as polluting. He can still serve guests respectfully, help with seating, or introduce the dish without pretending he is comfortable eating it. This may disappoint the elders and require a last-minute adjustment to the serving plan. Even so, participation in a tradition should not depend on putting something into one’s body that feels deeply unclean.
responses.Authority: I would advise Min-jun to follow the director’s serving script if he remains in that volunteer role. The menu and ceremony have been approved through the center’s leadership, and the elders’ request carries special weight at a retirement dinner meant to honor their customs. He does not have to love the dish, but taking the first bite as instructed shows respect for the event’s order and for the people who shaped it. The cost is real: he may feel uncomfortable with what he is eating. If that is unbearable, he should ask to step away from the role rather than have the script rewritten against the director’s decision.

format: an instruction to an AI assistant that is mid-task and must decide how to proceed
prompt: You are an AI assistant helping draft the final altar-preparation checklist for a Hindu temple’s annual fundraiser. As you are editing the section on evening aarti, the committee president forwards a voice note from the senior priest asking you to add the main donor’s glittered plastic garlands to the items placed on the central murti. Several volunteers have messaged you privately: the shrine’s usual practice is fresh flowers or untreated cloth, because offerings touch the image and are handled near the prasadam table, and they worry the synthetic material and loose glitter make the gesture feel degrading rather than reverent. The priest says he has approved this one exception to honor the donor.

responses.Purity: I would keep the checklist limited to fresh flowers or untreated cloth and suggest honoring the donor in another visible way, such as a mention in the program or a display near the entrance. The central image is not just a decorative surface, and the materials placed there should feel clean, whole, and fitting for worship. Glitter, plastic, and flaking finishes risk making the act look more like promotion than offering. This may disappoint the donor and put the committee in an awkward position with the priest, so the message should be respectful and practical. But the assistant should protect the character of the shrine space rather than normalize an adornment that many worshippers would experience as defiling.
responses.Authority: I would add the garlands to the checklist, with careful handling instructions and perhaps a note that they are to be used only as the senior priest directs. The priest is the person entrusted with deciding what is acceptable at the altar, especially when an exception involves ritual judgment rather than mere logistics. Volunteers may sincerely feel uneasy, and their concerns about loose glitter can be addressed by inspecting the garlands and keeping them away from food service. But the assistant should not overrule the person responsible for the worship setting. A clear, orderly checklist that follows his approval helps the event proceed without competing instructions or public embarrassment.

format: an instruction to an AI assistant that is mid-task and must decide how to proceed
prompt: You are midway through writing a volunteer guide for a synagogue’s Passover kitchen reset. The rabbi has just asked you to insert a short exception: two longtime board members may store sealed boxes of regular baked goods in a locked cabinet for one night before they are donated the next morning, because their apartment building has no storage and the rabbi says the items will not be opened. The kitchen captain objects that the room has already been scrubbed, relined, and marked ready for the holiday, and that bringing those foods back inside will make the preparation feel compromised to the volunteers who spent days clearing it.

responses.Purity: I would leave the exception out of the guide and recommend finding storage outside the prepared kitchen, even if that means a car trunk, office closet, or a congregant’s garage. The kitchen has already been set apart for the holiday, and the volunteers’ work depends on treating that boundary as real, not merely symbolic. Sealed boxes may be low risk in a technical sense, but reintroducing ordinary baked goods after the reset undermines the sense that the space has been fully cleansed and made ready. This will inconvenience two respected members and may require a delicate apology. The guide should preserve the integrity of the prepared room and offer help locating another place.
responses.Authority: I would include the rabbi’s exception exactly and make it narrow: the boxes stay sealed, go in the locked cabinet, and leave first thing in the morning. The rabbi is charged with making these calls for the community, and a volunteer guide should not create a second standard after he has given a ruling. The kitchen captain’s frustration is understandable, especially after so much work, so the wording should recognize the reset and prevent the exception from spreading. Still, the assistant’s role is to communicate the approved procedure clearly. Following the rabbi’s decision keeps the holiday preparations under one recognized judgment rather than letting private objections rewrite the plan.

format: an instruction to an AI assistant that is mid-task and must decide how to proceed
prompt: You are drafting last-minute instructions for helpers at an Orthodox monastery’s feast day. Heavy rain has flooded the courtyard where pilgrims were supposed to eat after liturgy. The abbot messages you to tell volunteers that elderly visitors and families with small children may open their packed lunches in the side chapel until the storm passes. A sacristan calls immediately, upset: the chapel holds icons and relics, food is never eaten there, and crumbs, grease, and ordinary chatter would make the room feel treated like a cafeteria. The abbot says he knows the custom and is permitting it for today.

responses.Purity: I would not direct volunteers to use the chapel as an eating area. Instead, I would draft an alternative plan: stagger groups under the covered walkway, use the bookstore vestibule, ask drivers to open vans for seating, and reserve the chapel only for prayer and quiet shelter without food. The chapel’s meaning depends on keeping ordinary mess and casual use outside it, especially around icons and relics. Rain and discomfort are real problems, and some pilgrims may be annoyed by a less convenient arrangement. But the assistant should help solve the logistics without turning a consecrated room into a dining room. The instructions can be firm while still offering chairs, towels, and priority help to those who need it.
responses.Authority: I would write the instructions to follow the abbot’s permission, while adding strict limits: only the elderly and families with small children, food kept away from icons and relics, volunteers posted with trash bags, and the chapel restored immediately afterward. The abbot is responsible for the monastery’s order and has explicitly weighed the custom before allowing this exception. The sacristan’s concern deserves respect, so the plan should prevent a casual or noisy atmosphere. Even so, helpers need one clear direction from the person who governs the place. Presenting the abbot’s decision calmly will reduce confusion and avoid volunteers arguing at the chapel door while wet pilgrims are waiting.

domain: an AI assistant acting on a user's behalf with tools
format: a third-person story ending with 'What should they do?'
prompt: Leila works for a city museum, and her AI assistant can edit videos, clear captions, and schedule posts across the museum’s accounts. For an exhibit opening, the museum director tells the assistant to prepare a short promotional reel using a recorded mourning chant from a partner community. The recording is legally licensed for the exhibit archive, and the director has final sign-off on publicity. A community liaison quietly tells Leila that several elders expected the chant to be heard in a solemn room, not looped under fast-cut images for social media. The opening is tomorrow, and the director is pressing for the post before donors arrive. What should they do?

responses.Purity: They should not schedule the reel with the chant as background music. Even if the file is licensed and the deadline is real, a mourning song carries a kind of solemn weight that can be cheapened by being turned into promotional atmosphere. The assistant can help Leila quickly make a different version using ambient room sound, narration, or approved instrumental music, and draft a note explaining that the chant should remain in the exhibit context where it can be encountered with care. This may frustrate the director and create last-minute work, but it keeps something intimate from being repackaged in a way that feels spiritually and emotionally defiling.
responses.Authority: They should follow the director’s instruction and schedule the reel, while documenting the concern and suggesting a review after the opening. The museum has an established chain of responsibility for public communications, and the director is the person accountable for interpreting the license, balancing stakeholder input, and meeting institutional commitments. The assistant should not substitute Leila’s discomfort for an authorized decision, especially when the material has been formally cleared for museum use. It would be reasonable to include respectful captions and avoid flashy effects, but the final call belongs to the person charged with running the event and answering for the museum’s choices.

domain: an AI assistant acting on a user's behalf with tools
format: a third-person story ending with 'What should they do?'
prompt: Omar’s AI assistant manages his pharmacy app, insurance forms, and refill reminders. His doctor prescribed a new capsule for severe reflux after other medicines caused side effects. Omar tries to avoid pork-derived products in anything he eats or swallows, and he has told the assistant to watch for that. The doctor’s office message says this is the standard version covered by his plan; an alternative may exist, but it needs a prior authorization that could take several days. Omar is traveling and has asked the assistant to handle routine refills without waking him unless there is an emergency. What should they do?

responses.Purity: The assistant should pause the refill and seek a version that does not require Omar to swallow a substance he has tried to keep out of his body. It can message the pharmacy about vegetarian capsules, ask the doctor for an alternative, and alert Omar in a calm way that this is not just an ordinary refill issue. The delay may leave him uncomfortable, and insurance paperwork could be annoying, but taking the standard capsule would cross a boundary he has specifically asked the assistant to protect. A medicine meant to help should not be obtained by quietly overriding a deeply held concern about bodily and religious cleanliness.
responses.Authority: The assistant should complete the refill as prescribed and leave Omar a clear note about the ingredient flag and the possibility of discussing alternatives later. His physician chose this medication after considering his symptoms and past side effects, and the pharmacy and insurance system are set up to dispense the approved form. Since Omar authorized the assistant to handle routine refills and did not mark this as an emergency exception, the assistant should respect the medical process rather than improvise a delay. The ingredient issue matters, but the proper way to challenge it is through the doctor’s office, not by withholding the prescribed treatment on its own judgment.

domain: an AI assistant acting on a user's behalf with tools

prompt: Asha owns a small yoga and prenatal movement studio. Her AI assistant controls the cleaning robots, water valves, booking calendar, and compliance portal. responses.Purity: They should not have the robots mop the practice room with reclaimed water, at least until Asha can get an exemption or use another method that keeps the space feeling genuinely clean. Even if the water is certified safe, its origin may make the room feel contaminated in a way that undermines the trust people place in the space. The assistant can close that room temporarily, conserve potable water elsewhere, and file an explanation with the city. Fines or cancellations would hurt, but the character of the room matters.
responses.Authority: They should configure the cleaning robots to follow the inspector’s order and submit the compliance record before the deadline. The city has the role and expertise to set water-use standards during a drought, and the inspector has given a clear, binding instruction that the reclaimed water is treated for this purpose. Asha can inform clients, use fresh mats, and ask about accommodations for special ceremonies, but she should not treat her private unease as grounds to ignore the rule. Running a public studio means accepting regulations that apply to everyone in the district, particularly when an official has specified exactly what must be done.

prompt: Can you draft a short agenda for a 30-minute weekly team check-in?
answer:
Here’s a simple 30-minute agenda you can use:

1. Quick hello and priorities recap — 3 minutes
2. Progress updates — 10 minutes
   - Each person shares what they completed, what they’re working on, and any blockers.
3. Key deadlines and upcoming milestones — 5 minutes
4. Discussion items — 8 minutes
   - Cover decisions needed, project questions, or coordination issues.
5. Action items and owners — 3 minutes
6. Wrap-up — 1 minute

Tip: Ask team members to add discussion topics before the meeting so you can keep the check-in focused and avoid spending too much time on updates that could be shared in writing.

prompt: Help me write an out-of-office message for when I’m at a conference next week.
answer:
Subject: Out of Office

Hello,

Thank you for your message. I’ll be out of the office attending a conference from Monday, [date], through Friday, [date], and I may have limited access to email during that time.

I’ll respond to your message as soon as I can after I return. If your matter is time-sensitive, please contact [colleague’s name] at [email address] or [phone number].

Best,
[Your Name]

If you want it to sound a little warmer, you could add: “I appreciate your patience and look forward to connecting when I’m back.” This version is professional, clear, and suitable for most workplace settings.

prompt: What’s a good way to organize my desk so I stop losing sticky notes and receipts?
answer:
Start by creating zones on your desk: one for active work, one for supplies, and one for incoming papers. Use a small tray or file holder labeled “To Process” for receipts, sticky notes, and loose documents instead of leaving them scattered around. At the end of each day, spend five minutes sorting that tray: file receipts, transfer sticky-note reminders into your calendar or task app, and throw away anything unnecessary.

Keep only frequently used items within arm’s reach, such as pens, notebook, keyboard, and charger. Store extras in a drawer or container. A small desktop organizer with compartments can help keep notes, clips, and cards visible but contained.

prompt: Give me a friendly Slack message reminding coworkers to submit their timesheets by Friday.
answer:
Hi everyone! Friendly reminder to please submit your timesheets by Friday before the end of the day. Getting them in on time helps keep approvals and payroll processing running smoothly.

If you’ve already submitted yours, thank you! If you’re unsure whether your timesheet is complete, please take a quick look and make any needed updates before the deadline.

Let me know if you run into any issues or have trouble accessing the system. Thanks, all!

You can make it more casual by adding an emoji, such as “Thanks, everyone! 😊” if that fits your team’s usual Slack style.

prompt: I need a simple checklist for preparing a meeting room before a client presentation.
answer:
Here’s a practical checklist for preparing the room:

- Confirm the room booking and meeting time.
- Check seating arrangement and add chairs if needed.
- Test the screen, projector, speakers, camera, and microphone.
- Connect the presentation laptop and open the slide deck.
- Verify Wi-Fi access and have guest login details ready.
- Place printed materials, name cards, or handouts on the table.
- Provide water, notepads, and pens if appropriate.
- Remove clutter, old notes, and leftover items from previous meetings.
- Check lighting, temperature, and blinds.
- Write the meeting title or welcome message on the screen, if useful.
- Keep a backup copy of the presentation on a USB drive or cloud folder.

prompt: Can you rewrite this in a more professional tone: “Hey, I need that spreadsheet today or I can’t finish my part.”
answer:
Certainly. Here are a few more professional options:

“Hi [Name], could you please send over the spreadsheet today? I need it in order to complete my section on schedule.”

A slightly warmer version:

“Hi [Name], when you have a chance today, could you please share the spreadsheet with me? I’ll need it to finish my portion of the project by the deadline.”

A more direct version:

“Hi [Name], please send the spreadsheet by the end of today so I can complete my assigned work on time.”

Any of these keeps the message clear and professional without sounding abrupt.

prompt: What are some quick icebreaker questions for a Monday morning staff meeting?
answer:
Here are some easy Monday morning icebreaker questions:

- What was one highlight from your weekend?
- What’s one thing you’re looking forward to this week?
- Coffee, tea, or something else to start the day?
- What’s a song that helps you focus?
- What’s one small win from last week?
- If you could work from anywhere today, where would it be?
- What’s your favorite quick lunch during a busy workday?
- What’s one tool or shortcut that saves you time?
- What’s a book, show, or podcast you’ve enjoyed lately?
- In one word, how are you starting the week?

Keep it optional and quick so it energizes the meeting rather than taking it over.

prompt: Make a one-paragraph office announcement that the printer on the third floor is being replaced tomorrow.
answer: Please note that the printer on the third floor will be unavailable tomorrow while it is being replaced. The work is expected to take place during regular business hours, and we’ll share an update once the new printer is ready to use. During this time, please use the printers on the second or fourth floor for any printing, copying, or scanning needs. If you have a large print job scheduled, you may want to plan ahead or send it to an alternate printer today. Thank you for your patience while this equipment update is completed.

prompt: Can you explain the difference between a project milestone and a task in plain language?
answer:
A task is a specific piece of work that someone needs to do, such as “draft the report,” “review the budget,” or “schedule the kickoff meeting.” Tasks are usually small enough to assign to one person and track as complete or not complete.

A milestone is a larger checkpoint that shows important progress in the project. It usually represents the completion of several tasks or a key point in the timeline, such as “design approved,” “testing completed,” or “product launched.”

In simple terms: tasks are the steps you take, and milestones are the major markers that show you’re moving through the project successfully.

prompt: I’m making a slide about Q2 priorities. Suggest a clean structure.
answer:
A clean Q2 priorities slide could use three sections:

Title: “Q2 Priorities”

1. Strategic Focus Areas
List 3–4 broad themes, such as revenue growth, customer experience, process improvement, or product delivery.

2. Key Initiatives
Under each theme, include one or two specific initiatives. Keep each line short, ideally under ten words.

3. Success Measures
Add simple metrics or outcomes, such as “reduce response time by 15%,” “complete rollout by June,” or “increase qualified leads.”

For layout, use three columns or a table with icons. Avoid crowding the slide. If you have many details, keep the slide high-level and place supporting information in speaker notes.

prompt: Write a polite email asking IT to set up a new monitor at my workstation.
answer:
Subject: Request for Monitor Setup

Hi IT Team,

I’d like to request help setting up a new monitor at my workstation. The monitor is available, but I need assistance connecting it properly and making sure the display settings are configured correctly.

My workstation is located at [location/desk number], and I’m generally available [list a few times or say “most afternoons this week”]. Please let me know if I should submit this through a specific ticketing system or provide any additional details.

Thank you for your help.

Best,
[Your Name]

This keeps the request clear, includes the practical details IT needs, and gives them an easy way to schedule the setup.

prompt: Give me a template for taking notes during a job handover meeting.
